# Results and limitations

**Synthetic Data — Analytical Simulation, Not Real Company Results.** All AI SaaS results below are generated by the documented model, seed 42, 10,000 accounts and 90 calendar days. No Monolit causal effect or business achievement is asserted.

## The observed model trade-off

| Scenario assumptions | Meaningful D7 difference | 30-day contribution difference per mature user | Model decision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Positive | +20.62 pp | $+1.863 | Advance to a real controlled pilot |
| Neutral | +19.89 pp | $+0.142 | Advance to a real controlled pilot |
| Negative | +17.28 pp | $-0.732 | Do not advance: economic guardrail harm |

Scenario names describe preset mechanisms, not fitted economic targets. All three use the same seed and assignment/channel draws; latent paths can differ because policy changes the RNG consumption order. These are unpaired model comparisons, not paired counterfactual estimates.

## Baseline uncertainty and eligible population

Control meaningful D7: 1.38%; treatment: 21.27%. Difference: +19.89 pp, 95% Newcombe interval [+18.67, +21.13] pp. Eligible accounts: 4,621 / 4,607. All assigned users: 5,011 / 4,989; SRM p=0.826.

First-30-day contribution difference is $+0.142 per mature user, 95% Welch interval [$-0.154, $+0.438]. This is uncertain economic uplift, not proven incremental profit. The pilot rule evaluates noninferiority against a predeclared illustrative −$0.25 tolerance, not superiority.

**A crucial interpretation boundary:** the default seven-day lifetime applies separately to each grant. Control's initial credit expires at the beginning of age 7; treatment's later grants can remain available until age 11. Thus the dramatic D7 contrast is partly a mechanical credit-availability effect at the selected checkpoint. It cannot isolate habit formation or value discovery. Timing, delivered entitlement, early subscription suppression of grants, and expiry are one bundled policy intervention. This is a reason to inspect D14/D30 and expiry sensitivity, not a real-world retention success story.

For a real pilot, decide explicitly whether to align the final expiry date across arms or compare the complete existing policies. Preregister a post-reward meaningful-use endpoint and billing guardrails, validate task outcomes, and recalculate power from actual historical baseline rates. The assumed planning baseline of 20% differs sharply from this model's realized control D7; neither is a real company estimate.

The planning target is 6,510 eligible accounts per arm for +2pp at an assumed 20% baseline, two-sided α=.05 and 80% power. This release is below that target. A very large mechanically induced synthetic difference can nevertheless be significant. Sample size does not repair model misspecification.

## Why retention is insufficient

The negative scenario increases meaningful D7 while harming first-30-day contribution. Its rule blocks advancing because of economic guardrails. More return behavior can coexist with lower paid demand, additional inference consumption or less sustainable economics. Neutral results do not establish a superior contribution margin: inspect raw arm margins and the contribution interval. Segment views are exploratory; apparent favorable subgroups require a prespecified interaction test or follow-up randomization.

## Independent real-data findings

The original UCI file contains 12,330 e-commerce sessions and 1,908 purchase sessions: 15.47% descriptive purchase conversion, 95% Wilson interval [14.85%, 16.12%]. Measured missing cells: 0; identical complete feature rows: 125. Without identity keys those rows are retained rather than labeled confirmed duplicates.

The source has long-tailed product-page duration (maximum 63,973.5; 99th percentile 8,701.1). Extremes are reported, not silently removed. Group confidence intervals expose small traffic-category samples. Returning versus new visitor comparisons are observational and may reflect selection, source mix or campaign differences, not a benefit of returning.

The purchase label is not money. There are no durable IDs, exact event timestamps or transaction amounts, so retention, ordered funnels, ARPU and causal treatment lift are not estimated from this file. Findings remain separate from the AI model. [Source, license and DOI](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/468/online+shoppers+purchasing+intention+dataset).

## Practical limits

Cash contribution omits CAC, payroll, hosting, tax, refunds and fees. Provider prices and return/purchase rules are illustrative. A session with zero successful requests is a low-value proxy, not an observed bonus-seeking motive. Two successful requests do not prove task completion. Signup-day sessions are modeled for every account, so first-30-day ever-active users equal eligible users in this release; calendar return trajectories and meaningful use provide more discrimination.

The release tests analytical correctness, explicit accounting and decision discipline. A/A calibration evaluates nominal false-positive behavior under a null simulation; it is not an instrumentation audit of a real product. Statistical intervals omit behavioral model uncertainty. Actual deployment status and test evidence live in docs/validation.md.

## Expiry sensitivity

Mean model differences across three seeds (42, 43, 44), 1,000 users per run. Only grant lifetime changes; these small unpaired scenario runs describe model sensitivity, not precise real-world effects.

| Credit lifetime | Meaningful D7 difference | Contribution difference per mature user |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 days | +0.71 pp | $-0.066 |
| 7 days | +21.32 pp | $+0.649 |
| 30 days | +3.73 pp | $+0.441 |

The much larger contrast at seven days supports investigating the checkpoint's mechanical dependence on the control credit-expiry boundary. It does not establish a durable habit effect.
